result.title: SHUSH: Emission-Aware Reward Design for Proactive Video Assistants
result.summary: Proactive video assistants must decide not only what to say, but also when to speak. Existing reinforcement-learning objectives can reward timely, correct responses without accounting for response volume, thereby encouraging unnecessary or repeated emissions. We identify this failure mode in MMDuet2, whose proactive area-under-the-curve (PAUC) reward promotes timely responses but does not price the number of emissions. We show analytically that this makes additional responses weakly penalized or effectively free, systematically encouraging over-emission. We then propose an emission-aware F1 reward for interval-valued annotations, using exclusive span--emission matching to price false emissions and missed spans. Under MMDuet2's training recipe, our policy on the visual subset of OmniPro replies 2.5x less often than MMDuet2 while raising timing F1 from 0.259 to 0.396 and content-aware F1 from 0.103 to 0.154; a more conservative variant cuts replies by 82.5% and raises precision from 0.161 to 0.418. On ProactiveVideoQA, the same reward adds replies where the baseline is nearly silent, and PAUC ranks a heavily over-emitting policy second despite near-last F1, because it is insensitive to response count. Our results indicate that proactive assistants should be trained and evaluated with objectives that price emissions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文分析 MMDuet2 中 PAUC 奖励不惩罚回复数量而导致过度发言，提出面向区间标注的 emission-aware F1 奖励，用互斥的片段—发言匹配同时惩罚误报与漏报，并在 OmniPro 视觉子集与 ProactiveVideoQA 上检验该奖励的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 对「发言次数」定价的奖励设计，以及不受次数影响的指标会高排过度输出策略这一诊断，可供核查是否能迁移到 LVR 中何时停止/输出（STOP）与证据获取成本的训练和评价。
